skill.name: bilibili-content-research
skill.description: Research public Bilibili videos and articles through SocialDataX, then summarize samples, title patterns, engagement signals, and topic ideas.
skill.summary: Turn keyword-based Bilibili search results into scoped content research reports.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: All 36 static matches are false positives involving Markdown, documented authentication, provider links, or readable multilingual text. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or concealed payloads in the supplied files. A separate medium concern is automatic execution of an unpinned npm package whose implementation is outside this review.

remediation.issue: The examples execute socialdatax-skills@latest through npx -y while the API key is available in the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and lock dependencies. Require approval before first execution, and isolate the CLI from unrelated credentials and files.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Execution of an Unpinned Third-Party CLI
semantic_findings.description: Both examples use npx -y socialdatax-skills@latest, which can download and execute changing npm code without an installation confirmation. The CLI runs with the provider API key available, so a compromised release could access credentials and local files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly combine @latest with -y, and the runtime instructions require an environment credential. Package compromise is a potential consequence, not observed malicious behavior.

content.user_title: Research Bilibili Videos and Content Ideas
content.value_statement: Bilibili content planning requires relevant samples and clear evidence boundaries. This skill uses SocialDataX search results to organize titles, engagement signals, and reusable topic ideas.
actual_capabilities: Search public Bilibili videos and articles by keyword using the SocialDataX CLI or corresponding MCP tools.
Apply documented sorting options and filter video samples by publication period or duration.
Collect bounded result pages with page and item limits, preserving partial results when requests fail.
Organize returned titles, authors, engagement metrics, publication times, URLs, and content IDs while marking missing fields.
Analyze title hooks and content angles, then suggest reusable topics and follow-up research questions.
limitations: Requires a SocialDataX API key, network access, and sufficient provider balance.
The direct CLI requires Node.js and npm; its implementation is not included in these skill files.
Results cover only selected keywords and returned pages, not all Bilibili content or verified platform-wide trends.
The documented workflow does not retrieve video transcripts or perform account login, posting, likes, or comments.

use_cases.title: Plan a Creator's Next Topics
use_cases.description: Compare relevant video titles and available engagement signals, then develop topic ideas grounded in the returned samples.

use_cases.title: Review Brand-Related Content
use_cases.description: Search brand and competitor keywords, preserve source links, and compare recurring content angles without claiming complete platform coverage.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Editorial Research Brief
use_cases.description: Collect video and article samples separately, identify title patterns, and document missing data and questions for further investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Find Initial Video Samples
prompt_templates.prompt: Search one page of Bilibili videos about [topic]. List returned titles, authors, and links, and mark missing fields.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Recent Video Angles
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Bilibili videos about [topic] from the past week, sorted by views. Limit results to 20 items. Compare title hooks and engagement signals.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: apply filters and compare samples.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Videos and Articles
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [brand or topic] using separate Bilibili video and article searches. Collect at most two pages each. Compare angles and propose five topics.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Bounded Research Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] across [keywords], with two pages and 30 items maximum per query. Preserve partial results and resume only with returned continuation tokens. Report scope, source IDs, missing fields, title patterns, engagement signals, and next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage multiple bounded queries and partial failures.

output_examples.input: Find one page of Bilibili videos about beginner photography and suggest content angles.
output: Illustrative report structure, not live search results.
Scope: beginner photography; one requested page; public results only.
Sample table: returned title, author, publication time, engagement metrics, full URL, and content ID.
Analysis: compare beginner questions, promised outcomes, and title specificity using the returned titles.
Next step: expand the strongest subtopic with a separate keyword search.

output_examples.input: Continue a research task after a partial API failure without duplicating earlier pages.
output: Illustrative recovery summary, not a live API response.
Status: incomplete; retain collected samples and the returned error.
Recovery: use a nonempty continuation token with the original query and remaining page and item allowances.
Stop if either limit is reached; do not restart automatically when a continuation token is missing.

best_practices: Start with one page and focused keywords, then expand only when the initial samples justify further requests.
Preserve source URLs and content IDs, disclose missing fields, and state the keyword and page scope of every conclusion.
Review and pin the CLI version before execution, protect the API key, and keep request limits within an approved budget.
anti_patterns: Treating a keyword sample as complete platform coverage or proof of a platform-wide trend.
Inventing missing engagement metrics, URLs, content IDs, or evidence about video content that was not retrieved.
Restarting partial searches from page one or repeatedly retrying balance errors, causing duplicate results and unnecessary charges.

faq.question: What can I provide as input?
faq.answer: Provide a keyword or topic direction. Add a brand, audience, or scenario to narrow the search.

faq.question: What setup does the direct CLI require?
faq.answer: It requires Node.js, npm, network access, and SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY. Review the npm package and approve execution before providing credentials.

faq.question: Can it search articles as well as videos?
faq.answer: Yes. Videos and articles use separate search commands or MCP tools. Publication-period and duration filters apply only to videos.

faq.question: Does the research cover all Bilibili results?
faq.answer: No. It covers the selected keywords and retrieved pages. Search has no stable complete-result boundary and does not support an all-results option.

faq.question: What happens when requests fail or balance is insufficient?
faq.answer: Keep partial samples and errors. Resume within the original limits using a returned token. Stop balance-error retries and direct users to provider billing.

faq.question: Does it log into or modify my Bilibili account?
faq.answer: The documented workflow searches public content through SocialDataX. It does not request browser data or perform login, posting, likes, comments, or account changes.
